decisions.check_result: Read-only git checks confirm the repository facts. git log --all -S basic_auth lists only b99bce4 (added) and 7345cc9 (removed). git show b99bce4:Caddyfile has basic_auth for user 'angel' with a 60-character $2a$14$M... bcrypt hash inside the intivision.online block. Scanning every commit in git rev-list --all finds the block in exactly eight commits (b99bce4, cfca76c, 89b2072, 747a21c, 352d16a, b11bddb, 1229858, 41b30dc), and git branch -a -v shows origin/chore/aplanar-bd_intivision at 747a21c. cfca76c only appended 'Caddyfile' to .gitignore, and 7345cc9 removed the hash and that entry at the tip. At b99bce4, backend/app.py routes had no authentication, and 8000:8000 dates from 2218cb2. The origin remote is a GitHub repository. The hash's presence is established, but any boundary result depends on facts outside source. Repository visibility is unverified, and if only the credential holders can read it, no lower-trust reader exists. The current HEAD Caddyfile, which is bind-mounted into guardian-caddy, has no basic_auth, and the app has its own login, so the hash guards nothing in current source unless the host's working copy still carries it. Whether the password is weak or reused is unknown. Because those unknowns are what make the exposure matter at all, needs_validation was chosen over confirmed. The record uses the hunter's fingerprint and root cause. Evidence for docker-compose.yml:60 was added, and the validation plan is now observation-only.

Every cited line was re-read at 5999fbf. docker-compose.yml:10 publishes 8000:8000 with no host IP. backend/Dockerfile:25 runs uvicorn on 0.0.0.0:8000 with no proxy flags. Caddyfile:2 already reaches backend:8000 internally. auth.py:239-240 trusts 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, loopback and fc00::/7. client_ip (auth.py:259-263) returns the last X-Forwarded-For element for such peers. That value keys the throttle at app.py:440 and 449 (default 30 failures per 15 minutes), the session ip at app.py:454 and the view_camera audit ip at app.py:731. cookie_is_secure (auth.py:203) and HSTS (app.py:157-158) depend on the scheme or X-Forwarded-Proto. Two facts narrow the impact. The per-account DB lockout (auth.authenticate) is unaffected by IP rotation. With the default Linux iptables DNAT the real public source is preserved, so the forged header is trusted only when Docker presents a private peer (docker-proxy for IPv6-to-IPv4 or local traffic, rootless or Desktop port drivers) or the client is on the server's private network. Whether 8000 is reachable, which peer address uvicorn sees, and whether anyone uses :8000 are deployment facts not in the repository. Nothing in source refutes the path, so it stays needs_validation. The record now mentions the account lockout and the DNAT case, and adds evidence at auth.py:283.
